newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack hatches station of the future.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack hatches station of the future.

text.p: Railtrack Plc, the rail infrastructure giant, has spent the last year locked in discussions with consultants to design the "ideal station" for customers -- a new concept offering franchises ranging from retailers to medical surgeries.

The station of the future could allow the passenger to buy a dental check-up while waiting for their trains, as well as a newspaper or cup of coffee. Railtrack's Bob Hill, head of property, told a press briefing "At the moment it's an embryonic plan. We want to create a generic type which can be used to serve all needs."
Hill said an ideal station for each passenger region could be created out of a "kit of parts."
He said in future revenues from these kind of outlets would be important to Railtrack, but would not eclipse its true business of generating rail traffic on its network.
"Although we don't benefit from bums on seats. We do benefit from trains on track and we are in the business of encouraging rail usage," said Hill.
While it is Railtrack's job to develop train traffic and the infrastructure, the job of raising passenger numbers lies with the train operating companies who run the rail services.
Some trial franchise operations are already underway in key stations. For instance, a doctor's surgery operates out of London Victoria and is highly profitable, said Railtrack.
It is even considering partnership with some private companies to develop this side of the business. Though nothing is set in stone at this stage.
